guṇātīta
(‘one [who is] beyond [the sway of the three] guṇas’)
------------------------------------------
The quest for perfection has been a common characteristic feature of all religions and philosophical systems. Since perfection is only a concept, it can best be understood only when concretised through a person or a personality. The Bhagavadgītā has done this in three places (vide 2.55-72; 12.13-20 and 14.22-27). The ‘guṇātīta’ is the last of these three.
The गुणातीत is the one who has transcended the three guṇas—sattva, रजस् and तमस्. He is unmoved by the effects of the three guṇas (like knowledge or action or delusion). He is equanimous in happiness or misery. He looks upon a clod of earth or stone or gold as of equal worth—being neither repelled nor tempted by them—and is unmoved by the pleasant and the unpleasant or praise and blame. He treats friends and enemies equally, based on the merits of the case. He serves God with undeviating love. Such an one is fit to attain ब्रह्मन्.

guṇa
(‘quality’)
------------------------------------------
One of the most widely used words, ‘guṇa’ has several senses such as quality, rope, bow-string, nature and certain letters of the Sanskrit alphabet used in grammar. However, in the Indian philosophical systems such as Sāṅkhya, योग and Vedānta it refers to the three fundamental components of प्रकृति or प्रधान or māyā, the basic matrix out of which the physical universe is created.
These guṇas are three in number: सत्त्व, रजस् and तमस्.
They are not qualities or attributes in any sense, but fundamental subtle substances or elements which constitute the प्रकृति like three cords making a rope.
The existence of these guṇas is inferred from the qualities presented in the created world. सत्त्व is responsible for knowledge and pleasure. रजस् is responsible for activity and passions. तमस् produces indolence, sleep and evil.
Before च्रेअतिओन्, these three are in a perfectly balanced state. At the beginning of च्रेअतिओन्, this balance is upset and evolution of the world starts.
See SĀṄKHYA DARŚANA for more details.
In the न्याय and Vaiśeṣika systems, ‘guṇa’ is described as a quality or an attribute. Guṇas are 24 in number. Some of them are: rūpa (shape), गन्ध (odour), saṅkhyā (number), saṁyoga (conjunction), gurutva (weight), icchā (desire), धर्म (merit) and so on.
In Sanskrit literature ten guṇas or excellences of a composition, are listed. For instance, prasāda (clarity), samatā (uniformity in the type of clusters of consonants used), udāratva (decency and dignity of the subject), kānti (loveliness of expression) are some of these.
The word when used to indicate the policies of a state refers to six measures such as सन्धि (alliance), vigraha (war) and आसन (neutrality), adopted by the State.
